newsitem.title: UK: Crude tankers for UK-Cont up on end-month squeeze.
newsitem.headline: Crude tankers for UK-Cont up on end-month squeeze.

text.p: North Sea crude tanker rates firmed on Tuesday as charterers scrambled for tonnage for the end of the month, but the rest of the market was generally flat.
"We're seeing rates as high as W115 for UK-cont trips for the end of the month," said one broker, referring to Wintershall's fixing of the 80,000 tonne Bona Rainbow loading in Sture on February 27.
"It's not unusual to see rates rise as the end of a loading period approaches and charterers start worrying they won't find vessels," he added.
Most brokers saw rates easing back to the W90s range by the beginning of March.
There was also mounting interest in the sector for vessels going to the United States.

Sun were reported to have fixed the 135,000 tonne North Star for a trip from Norway to the U.S. Atlantic Coast loading March 2 at a rate of W84.5, and brokers said a number of players had made enquiries about vessels for transatlantic journeys.
Oil brokers said Brent could attract U.S. interest if the spread between IPE April Brent and NYMEX crude held above $1.50 a barrel. It stood at $1.54 at 1646 GMT on Tuesday.
Elsewhere, the markets were fairly dull.
Middle East rates weakened to W60-62.5 for VLCCs on Middle East-Japan trips, while vessels headed for Thailand from the Middle East.
The Mediterranean was also weaker. Exxon was reported to have fixed the 140,000 tonne White Sea for a trip from Sidi Kreir to Augusta for W85.

The Caribbean to U.S. coast market remained in the doldrums with a 70,000 tonne vessel on such a route typically commanding W112.5-115. "There's a lot of tonnage and not many cargoes," said one broker. It doesn't look good." -- London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7714.
